```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

This guide produces prices and default-risk comparisons for one small debt-financed
merger. It needs `financial` 0.1.0 and compatible `antitrust` (at least 0.99.43),
including the ordinary `cubature` dependency. It does no Bayesian estimation and
needs no CmdStan installation. Install the package before running these chunks;
installation is not part of the calculation.

## Fit and re-solve the small market

The three products initially have separate owners. Owner `"1"` buys product 2;
the product-row payment contributions are unchanged. All margins are finite and
expressed as proportions of price. This is the valid single-market example used
by the package's debt lifecycle tests, rather than a historical multi-market
diagnostic fixture.

```{r debt-fit}
fit <- financial::debt_fit(
  prices = c(10, 10, 10), shares = c(.3, .3, .4),
  margins = c(.5, .5, .5),
  ownerPre = c("1", "2", "3"), ownerPost = c("1", "1", "3"),
  debtPre = c(.5, .5, .5), mktSize = 1, density = "beta"
)
result <- antitrust::simulate(fit)
price_table <- data.frame(
  product = 1:3,
  pre = antitrust::calcPrices(result@model, preMerger = TRUE),
  post = antitrust::calcPrices(result@model, preMerger = FALSE)
)
price_table$change <- price_table$post - price_table$pre
knitr::kable(price_table, digits = 4,
             caption = "Price levels and post-minus-pre changes (currency per unit).")
```

`debt_fit()` calibrates the model **and solves the supplied post ownership**.
`simulate(fit)` re-solves that stored scenario; it is not a second acquisition.
To study a different single-step scenario, pass a new `ownerPost` and, if needed,
`debtPost` to `simulate()` using the originating fit. The legacy constructor
`logit.debt()` instead returns the inner `LogitDebt` model directly. Here
`fit@model` holds that model and `fit` is the lifecycle wrapper.

Read price changes as levels in the same currency as the input price; divide by
the pre price for a proportional change. Do not interpret the merger as a change
in marginal cost: debt affects conditional incentives through limited liability.

## Keep products, firms and payment units distinct

The input shares describe the product allocation conditional on the relevant
market participation/default structure. In this example they sum to one. They
are not a separate draw of the stochastic outside share. The Beta outside-share
law is calibrated by the debt model using the observed prices and complete
product margins. An ordinary unconditional inside-share vector is not a
drop-in replacement for these observations.

| Input | Meaning and unit |
| --- | --- |
| `prices` | Currency per physical product unit |
| `shares` | Product quantity shares under the debt model's conditioning |
| `margins` | `(price - marginal cost) / price`, one finite proportion per product |
| `mktSize` | One physical market-size scale per market, consistent with profit/payment levels |
| `debtPre`, `debtPost` | Currency payment contributions on product rows, summed by owner |
| `ownerPre`, `ownerPost` | Product-row firm identifiers in each scenario |

For a multiproduct firm, allocate its payment across its rows rather than repeat
the whole firm payment on each row. The model sums contributions using the
applicable pre or post owner vector. This arithmetic illustration does not fit
another market:

```{r debt-aggregation}
payment_rows <- data.frame(owner = c("A", "A", "B"), payment = c(.2, .3, .5))
aggregate(payment ~ owner, payment_rows, sum)
```

Firm A's payment is .5, not 1. The tutorial merger similarly combines the two .5
contributions under owner `"1"`. Set market size and payment currency together:
rescaling quantities without rescaling debt changes default incentives.

## Interpret default and survival changes

```{r default-results}
u <- result@diagnostics$uncertainty_delta
stopifnot(is.null(u$error))
default_table <- data.frame(
  firm = u$firm,
  default_pre = unname(u$default_prob_pre),
  default_post = unname(u$default_prob_post),
  default_change = unname(u$delta_default_prob),
  survival_change = unname(u$delta_survival_mass)
)
knitr::kable(default_table, digits = 5,
             caption = "Probabilities and post-minus-pre probability changes.")
```

The probability columns use the interval 0 to 1; multiply a change by 100 to
report percentage points. A negative default change is a reduction in the
reported default probability. The survival-mass change has the opposite sign.
Owner `"2"` is absorbed, so its post value and its difference are `NA`, not zero.
The surviving owner's post portfolio includes both merging products, whereas
its pre comparison is that owner's own pre portfolio. This is a firm-indexed
comparison, not a portfolio-matched causal decomposition.

In this example the merging owner benefits from pooled conditional profits;
the table supplies the calculated sign. Other inputs need not produce the same
price or default-risk direction. The calibrated Beta law stays fixed in this
single-step calculation. Changing ownership or payment exposure is different
from introducing a new uncertainty primitive.

```{r debt-identities}
defined <- is.finite(u$delta_default_prob) & is.finite(u$delta_survival_mass)
stopifnot(
  all(is.finite(price_table$post)),
  all(u$default_prob_post[is.finite(u$default_prob_post)] >= 0),
  all(u$default_prob_post[is.finite(u$default_prob_post)] <= 1),
  max(abs(u$delta_default_prob[defined] + u$delta_survival_mass[defined])) < 1e-8,
  identical(fit@parameters, result@parameters)
)
```

These assertions check extraction and probability accounting. They do not
independently certify a profit-maximizing equilibrium. The package's economic
tests additionally check the single-market default/Beta identities against
independent calculations.

## Numerical failures and supported limits

Undefined default conditioning raises `financial_zero_survival`; quadrature
that fails its error bounds raises `financial_integration_failure`; unverified
calibration or price roots raise `financial_equilibrium_failure`. Inspect the
condition and input units before interpreting a failed scenario. Finite prices
alone are not a certificate, and matching an invalid historical result is not
economic validation. Debt calibration requires every product margin to be finite.

| Operation | Debt family |
| --- | --- |
| Construct from observed inputs | `debt_fit()`; legacy inner-model route `logit.debt()` |
| One fitted-state scenario | `simulate()` with ownership/payment exposure changes |
| Sequential paths | `simulate_steps()` is unsupported |
| Switch model/uncertainty primitives | `respecify()` is unsupported; no generic uncertainty-step workflow |

There is no general `calibrate()`/`specify()` registry route for this family.
See `?financial::logit.debt` for arguments and `?financial::"DebtFit-lifecycle"`
for the lifecycle contract. For the separate bank pricing/liquidity question,
read [Bank merger rates and liquidity pooling](bank-liquidity-merger.html) in
the rendered collection. If reading this Rmd source, use the
[bank guide source](https://github.com/luciu5/financial/blob/main/vignettes/bank-liquidity-merger.Rmd)
instead; built bundles also provide
`vignette("bank-liquidity-merger", package = "financial")`.
